subject: bkmr updated to 7.6.7; vault-root ingest and --room-depth take unresolved links from 2338 to 150
result: Follow-up to tags-leave-the-wiki-node-namespace-2026-09-08, closing its open items (1) and (4-bkmr). BKMR UPDATED: the machine carried bkmr 6.5.0 at /usr/local/bin, below the 7.6.7 conformance target and without the --db selector the adapter requires, so surface_reason() withheld the provider entirely. Installed bkmr 7.6.7 (cargo install bkmr --locked, ~/.cargo/bin, which precedes /usr/local/bin on PATH) and moved the stale binary aside to /usr/local/bin/bkmr-6.5.0.superseded so exactly one bkmr resolves. VERIFIED against the real binary, not a fake runner: `--db` exists; hierarchical corpus tags round-trip verbatim (`bkmr --db ... add ... "source-bank/record,source-bank/jung"` then `search --tags source-bank/jung --json` returns exactly that row); and 7.6.7's search --json emits a FLAT bookmark array rather than the {bookmark,score} envelope the adapter's fixtures use — hit_from_record's `.get("bookmark").unwrap_or(record)` already handles both, so no adapter change was needed. bkmr also injects its own `_imported_` tag, which is harmless because the filter is subset-based. LINK RESOLUTION — the address space was diagnosed, not guessed. There is exactly ONE symbolon folder; the suspicion of duplicates is unfounded. The real condition is three separate faults, measured per link: (a) 610 links pointed at files that exist in the vault and resolve normally but declared NO identity — the corpus's own most-cited documents (SOURCE-INDEX 187 inbound, PASSAGE-LEDGER 138, the ROOM pages, WHOLE-FIELD 265, MOC) carried none at all; (b) 275 links carried a redundant `submission-package/essay/` prefix — a repo-relative address for the vault root, unresolvable from inside it — a half-finished migration an earlier session had started; (c) ~110 genuinely point outside the vault into working/ or are dead display names. The vault root is settled evidence, not opinion: `.obsidian` lives at submission-package/essay and nowhere else, and `.bkmr/manifest.tsv`'s 884 canonical_paths all resolve inside it. So ingest is pointed there. ROOM DEPTH: reading from the vault root collapsed 17 room spaces to 1, because a room was always the first path segment and from there every record is under `symbolon/`. Added `wiki ingest --room-depth N` (default 1) — a room is relative to the root ingest was pointed at, and the depth says which root is being read. Depth 2 from the vault recovers symbolon/episteme, symbolon/mytheme, symbolon/matheme. MEASURED, vault root + depth 2, 823 files: records 328, sources 495, source bindings 823, skipped_inert 0, skipped_unaddressable 0, duplicate ids 0, tag vocabulary 190, tagged bindings 609, spaces 3, edges 3261, UNRESOLVED LINKS 2338 -> 150. The 150 remaining are honest: 110 address working/ outside the vault, 40 are display names or dead notes. Plus 24 declared source_ids naming no source page. TESTS: 696 pass; the one failure is the pre-existing tmux mux_install test, confirmed on a stashed tree. PRODUCT-GROUND: wiki-write and gateway re-reconciled for the room-depth change; errors back to the same 7 pre-existing main-debt entries. FOUND, NOT FIXED — a real duplication the owner should rule on. The essay repo carries its own complete parallel knowledge system: tools/okf-workspace.py (1644 lines) implements discover/resolve/edges/find/links/backlinks/neighbourhood/path over the same corpus and builds six SQLite databases under .bkmr/db from .bkmr/manifest.tsv (884 rows: passages 536, records 179, concepts 89, sections 48, arguments 21, rooms 11). That is the same job AIKit's SemanticWiki + SourcePool now does, over the same files, feeding the same tool. Its identity rule is primary_id(): source_id for a source house, notes-<dir>, room-<dir>, reading-<dir>, else the filename stem — the SAME rule this session declared into the files, so the two do not conflict on identity; the manifest's doc_id is that value with a collection prefix, a derived build artefact rather than a competing register. But two implementations and two bkmr indexes over one corpus is duplication, and retiring one is the owner's call, not a side effect of this PR. OPEN: (1) decide okf-workspace.py/.bkmr vs AIKit ingest — they now do the same job. (2) The 110 links into working/ want a decision about whether working/ is corpus. (3) Still uncommitted on ai-kit main (now 49bff02) — wants a branch and a PR. (4) The 7 pre-existing product-ground errors.
